post.caption: Topaz may be named for peridot's island. Most authorities say its name comes from Topazios, a Red Sea island that is now called Zabargad. The island never produced topaz, and its stone was probably peridot. Imperial topaz is a rich golden to reddish-orange color, and it comes from near Ouro Preto in Brazil. The name imperial honors royalty, though sources disagree on which royal. Most blue topaz is colorless topaz treated with radiation and heat. Topaz is hard at 8, yet it can split along one plane. The American Golden Topaz weighs 22,892 carats.
